entries.situation: Useful intensity ranges are unknown and the user wants to design a transfer function, inspect structures, or reduce visual noise.
entries.goal: Map normalized intensity bins to visible structures and artifacts, then use the map to choose color and opacity ranges.

guidance.text: Use the sweep once before building a transfer function for an unfamiliar scalar channel or removing noise whose intensity is unknown. Reuse a prior report for the same dataset scope and channel whenever it answers the question. Match each relevant intensity bin to its numbered preview: note the wanted structures, background or likely noise. Do not infer a structure from coverage or a noise hint alone, especially if the preview image is no longer available. Then design the transfer function from this bin-to-structure map: assign colors to useful structures, keep opacity zero in intervals dominated by noise or background that contain nothing wanted, and preserve useful detail. Verify the combined result with a rendered view. Repeat the sweep only when a specific unresolved question needs new evidence.

procedure.announcement_hint: Briefly say what you are looking for in the dataset, using everyday language. Do not describe the method or comment on whether the view will change.

difference_threshold.description: Fraction of all image pixels whose visibility changes between adjacent bands. Lower this for small details.

bins.description: Each measured intensity bin, its coverage, qualitative noise hints and numbered preview when visible.
